ratings.concept: Electrons supplied per mole in a permanganate titration: count the oxidation-state change of the cation AND of the anion (Fe2+ → Fe3+, oxalate → CO2, sulphite → sulphate, nitrite → nitrate)
ratings.strategy_evidence: Sulphate is already the fully oxidised sulphur anion, so FeSO4 can give only the single Fe2+ → Fe3+ electron while every other salt also has an oxidisable anion; that one fact strikes options 1, 2 and 4.

traps.label: omitted_contribution
traps.route: leaves out the two electrons from oxalate → 2CO2 and counts only Fe2+ → Fe3+, which makes FeC2O4 (really 3 electrons per mole) tie with the key at 1 electron

traps.label: semantic_reversal
traps.route: Fe(NO2)2 needs the most permanganate, not the least: 1 electron for Fe2+ → Fe3+ plus 2 electrons for each NO2− → NO3− is 5 per mole, so the option answers the stem with "least amount" read as greatest

traps.label: omitted_contribution
traps.route: leaves out the two electrons from SO3^2− → SO4^2− and counts only Fe2+ → Fe3+, which makes FeSO3 (really 3 electrons per mole) tie with the key

ratings.reason: This question requires computing and comparing the electron demand of four salts, demonstrated by the stem "same moles of which of the following compounds will require the least amount of acidified KMnO4 for complete oxidation?" with FeSO4, whose anion cannot be oxidised further, as the key.

traps.label: wrong_quantity

group_note: The packet was grouped on structure=plain and four members are plain_mcq, but two do not belong with the rest and it matters: q014 and q041-style items are structure-option questions — in q014 every option is a drawn alkene — and they were read as "plain" only because our record replaced each option image with the text "[structure diagram]". q014 is therefore recorded with the verdict source_damage_artifact and an empty traps list, and its E4 labels are taken from the stem alone, which names both the rule and the product; the damage is described in its note rather than tagged as the question's shape (rulebook section 7). Among the six, consistency was kept by demand rather than by appearance: the two naming/convention items get application because a stated convention decides them (q018 electronegativity decides "oxide of fluorine", q019 the IUPAC rules decide the name), the two reagent-and-value items get recall because one stored fact decides them (q016 the Reimer–Tiemann product, q017 the 68% bcc packing fraction), and q015 alone gets calculation because electron counts are computed and compared. solution_structure follows the same discipline: several_independent_checks where every option must be adjudicated before one can be chosen (q014, q015, q018), single_step where one stored fact or one naming act settles it (q016, q017, q019) — four options adjudicated are not four dependent steps. elimination is carried only by q015, where a named fact (sulphate cannot be oxidised further) strikes three options; the others offer four same-kind options and no shortcut was demonstrable. On E5 the negated item q018 gets true_statement_trap on each true statement with the polarity named, while the rest carry option-specific devices; new_trap is used once, for the 23%/32% digit-reversal decoy in q017, because no live label covers a transposed-digit option.
